newsitem.title: USA: "60 Minutes" says Nazi symbols found at Citadel.
newsitem.headline: "60 Minutes" says Nazi symbols found at Citadel.

text.p: The CBS news programme "60 Minutes" Friday said students at The Citadel displayed Nazi and Ku Klux Klan symbols despite the military college's statements that it would never condone such actions.

In a report to be aired Sunday, "60 Minutes" said the publicly financed South Carolina college has a decades-old tradition of displaying Nazi and KKK symbols. A photograph in a 1977 yearbook shows cadets in KKK garb surrounding a black man with a noose around his neck, it said.
The report includes an interview with a black former student who was shot on campus and says the incident was racial.

An interview with a woman student who quit the school after being subjected to hazing for failing to know the name of an extreme KKK faction was also to be aired. The woman, Jeannie Menavlos, said male cadets set her clothes on fire.
The Citadel refused to be interviewed for the report but its interim president, Clifton Poole, last month said charges that Nazi symbols were displayed on campus "lacked any basis in fact."
The programme said it obtained photographs and videos taken this spring showing a Nazi SS symbol on a student's cap and a picture in a locker of a boy giving the "Heil Hitler" salute.
